messages.author: 2368ae49227cd233
messages.subject: Modification Indices with ~*~  Operator
parts:
Hi,

When I compare two groups of ordinal data using CFA model, I also checked what indices needed to be modified.

Some operations that stood out included (indicator1 ~*~  indicator1). I sort of understand this operator has something to do with scaling and reparameterization. But how am I supposed to modify the model to ameliorate this effect brought about by ~*~? Thank you very much.

Best,
Chao

messages.author: 3fe90052fbf2f899
messages.subject: Re: Modification Indices with ~*~  Operator
parts: (indicator1 ~*~  indicator1). I sort of understand this operator has something to do with scaling and reparameterization.

Correct, it is similar to fixing the scale of a common factor so the model is identified, but this is about identifying scale of the latent item response underlying indicator1. You would only be able to free it if you placed appropriate constraints on other parts of the model.  The typical circumstance would be multigroup or longitudinal models, where invariance constraints allow those parameters to be separately identifiable for estimation.  You can read details here:

https://www.statmodel.com/download/webnotes/CatMGLong.pdf

http://dbauer.web.unc.edu/files/2014/08/kamata-bauer-2008.pdf

dx.doi.org/10.1037/1082-989X.9.3.301
how am I supposed to modify the model to ameliorate this effect brought about by ~*~?

You can free it the same way you would free other parameters:

indicator1 ~*~  NA*indicator1

http://lavaan.ugent.be/tutorial/syntax2.html

But again, you probably don't want to consider freeing those parameters unless they will be identified.

Terrence D. Jorgensen
Postdoctoral Researcher, Methods and Statistics
Research Institute for Child Development and Education, the University of Amsterdam
UvA web page: http://www.uva.nl/profile/t.d.jorgensen
